Ordered by projected final RPI position. “Prev” is the same team’s position in the prior week’s run. Each week was simulated from the results available at that date (earlier weeks were re-run from the game history), so movement reflects that week’s results. Every team with a real chance at an at-large bid, ordered from most to least likely within each category. Automatic-bid favorites are listed only if they are not safe. Tick the box on any row to compare teams side by side.

Tracks conference-tournament season and the NCAA’s .500 rule for at-large bids (a .500 or better record and 11+ games). Teams that cannot reach .500 are struck through everywhere on this page; they keep their data, and those with no tournament path are dropped from the bubble list.

Pick two to four bubble teams. Teams are ranked by their overall chance of an at-large bid, with what each needs from its own games and from games elsewhere.

Automatic-bid favorites. Conference tournaments themselves are not simulated, but only teams that can still make a league’s tournament field can win its automatic bid. Each simulation draws the champion from the simulated final conference standings (points per game) and in-conference RPI rank, fitted on 2022–25 (the regular-season leader won 36% of the time, the second-place team 31%).

Method and limits

  • RPI rebuilt from game results with the NCAA formula and non-conference bonus/penalty table; matches the NCAA adjusted values (correlation 0.998).
  • Team ratings from an ordered-logit model anchored on last year's rank; remaining games simulated 3,000 times.
  • At-large model: logistic regression on RPI rank, SoS rank, non-conference opponent strength, conference strength, and two gaps — Massey rank vs RPI rank and Top-50 results rank vs RPI rank (added Oct 12, 2026) — trained on every committee field 2007–2025. The gaps capture teams whose results are better or worse than their RPI says; they raised the leave-one-year-out score from 90.8% to 91.8% and cut probability log loss by about 16%.
  • Massey and Top-50 results ranks are rebuilt from game results and simulated with the RPI (they match the published sheets at 0.98 and 0.93–0.95 rank correlation, so live values are close but not identical).
  • Weekly trend: each weekly run is saved as a snapshot. Arrows compare with the snapshot at least six days earlier. Earlier weeks (from Sep 6) were re-simulated from the results available at those dates, so they use the same model but with the information of that date.
  • Conference tournaments themselves are not simulated, but only teams that can still make a league’s tournament field can win its automatic bid; neutral sites are untagged; a few teams have small game-count gaps vs the NCAA table; selection day expected Mon Nov 16, 2026 (the NCAA moved the 2026 schedule a week later).
